author: evolve
description: Curated bundle for a project-manager bot. Installs the four behaviors that keep a project's threads from dropping — Task Manager, Meeting Note-taker, Commitment Tracker, Pre-Meeting Brief — along with their data-layer foundations (Contacts, Calendar Sync). Meta-spec only: installs the six dependencies, ships no scripts of its own. This is the project-manager archetype's starter pack for the add-bot wizard (starter-pack + archetype-project-manager tags).
name: Project Pack

app_dependencies.reason: Foundation data layer. Persistent task registry with owners, priorities, and approval states — the project's source of truth for open work.
Foundation data layer. Per-person relationship memory; Commitment Tracker stores commitments here and Pre-Meeting Brief draws attendee context from it.
Foundation data layer. Local calendar cache; Pre-Meeting Brief reads its memory/calendar-today.json and memory/calendar-upcoming.json.
Behavior: capture surface. Turns meeting conversations into structured notes and action items the project can act on.
Behavior: conversation-driven surface. Captures commitments made in conversation into Contacts memory and surfaces overdue ones once per day.
Behavior: calendar-driven surface. Briefing ~60 minutes before each external meeting, with attendee context drawn from Contacts.

identity.purpose: Package the four project-manager behaviors plus their two data-layer foundations as one installable unit, so an operator (or the add-bot wizard) can choose 'the project bundle' instead of picking six apps individually. The meta-spec itself has no behavior — every note, brief, and follow-up belongs to a downstream app. Removing this meta-spec would not remove any capability; it would only require installing the six dependencies one at a time.
scope_includes: Declare a strict app_dependencies graph that the installer resolves into the six underlying apps, foundations before behaviors
Carry the starter-pack tags (starter-pack, archetype-project-manager) that let the add-bot wizard discover this bundle for the project-manager role
Carry the operator-facing description for the bundle (its name, blurb, and tag set), nothing more
scope_excludes: Installing any script of its own — every script lives in a downstream app
Declaring scheduled_actions of its own — every cron / heartbeat instruction belongs to a downstream app
Declaring integrations of its own — every integration is required transitively through Calendar Sync (Google Calendar)
Overriding configuration of downstream apps — each downstream app reads its own network.json::capabilities block
identity.bot_interaction_pattern: None — this is a meta-package, not a runtime app. The bot never invokes anything labeled 'project-pack'; it invokes the underlying behavior apps directly.
identity.user: The operator at install time (directly or via the add-bot wizard's starter-pack proposal). After install completes, Project Pack is invisible at runtime — every actual note, brief, and follow-up is surfaced by one of the downstream apps.

observable_outcomes: Selecting Project Pack installs all six dependencies in the correct order (foundations before behaviors)
After install, each of the four behavior apps shows as `status: active` in the bot's apps list with its own scheduled_actions and interface_contract
The add-bot wizard's project-manager proposal resolves this bundle's dependency list as the proposed starter set
Uninstalling Project Pack only removes the meta-spec from the bot's apps list — downstream apps remain installed and continue to function
failure_signals: Project Pack installs but only N of 6 dependencies appear in the bot's apps list — installer dependency resolution is incomplete
Two downstream apps disagree on a shared file's format — the contract between behaviors and foundations has drifted
Behavior apps install but their scheduled_actions don't fire — plists or HEARTBEAT.md sections were not materialized

quality_bar.minimum: Project Pack is a strict superset of its dependencies — installing it produces exactly the same bot capability set as installing the six apps manually, in the same order.
quality_bar.excellent: An operator who knows nothing about Evolve's apps-as-contracts framing can pick 'Project Pack' (or accept the wizard's proposal) and within one day have meeting notes captured, commitments tracked, and pre-meeting briefs arriving with attendee context.

privacy: Project Pack carries no data of its own — every privacy obligation passes through to a downstream app. See the Contacts spec for relationship-memory privacy, Calendar Sync for calendar-data handling, and Meeting Note-taker for conversation-capture boundaries.
safety: The meta-spec declares no scripts and no scheduled actions, so it cannot fail at runtime. The downstream apps' safety constraints apply individually.

Installer must resolve dependencies in topological order: data-layer apps (Task Manager, Contacts, Calendar Sync) before behavior apps. A behavior app installed without its foundation will emit a *_FAILED: signal on its first run.
dependencies: All six dependencies above are REQUIRED. There is no degraded mode where Project Pack works without one of them — the bundle's value is the full project rhythm in one install.

If an operator wants only a subset (e.g. task tracking without meeting prep), they should install those apps individually — or trim the set in the add-bot wizard's proposal, which installs the apps directly rather than this bundle.
boundaries: Project Pack does not introduce a network.json::capabilities.project_pack config block — each downstream app reads its own capabilities block.
Project Pack does not own any HEARTBEAT.md section — every heartbeat instruction belongs to a downstream app's scheduled_actions.
Project Pack version bumps are only required when the dependency graph changes (a behavior added, a dependency renamed, a required→optional flip).

build_spec:
# Project Pack — Build Specification

## Overview

This is a **meta-package**. It declares no files of its own; the installer is expected to resolve `app_dependencies` and install each downstream app independently.

There is nothing for forge to build at install time. The Build phase is a no-op:

- No scripts to write.
- No data files to seed.
- No plists or HEARTBEAT.md sections to materialize.
- No openclaw.json mutations.

If the installer ships Project Pack to a bot and the six dependencies are already installed, the bot's apps list gains an `app_project_pack` entry whose only content is the metadata above (description, tags, identity, dependency list). Removing the Project Pack entry removes only that metadata.

## Dependency graph

```
  Meeting Note-taker ─┐
  Commitment Tracker ─┼── depend on ──┐
  Pre-Meeting Brief ──┘                ├── Task Manager  (foundation)
                                       ├── Contacts      (foundation)
                                       └── Calendar Sync (foundation)
```

- **Foundation apps** (Task Manager, Contacts, Calendar Sync) own data formats and CLIs.
- **Behavior apps** (Meeting Note-taker, Commitment Tracker, Pre-Meeting Brief) own the captures and briefs that read the foundation data and deliver via `openclaw message send`.

## Install order (installer responsibility)

The installer must apply dependencies in topological order — foundations first, then behaviors:

```
1. Task Manager (p-9bfa1c84)
2. Contacts (p-4136a932)
3. Calendar Sync (p-fe9acef3)
4. Meeting Note-taker (p-f14e9562)
5. Commitment Tracker (p-3b4f5d29)
6. Pre-Meeting Brief (p-2c7a9b6e)
```

## Starter-pack role

This bundle is the **project-manager archetype's starter pack** for the conversational add-bot wizard (docs/spec-add-bot-wizard-build-delta-2026-06-10.md §5). The wizard discovers it via the `starter-pack` + `archetype-project-manager` tags, proposes the dependency list as the new bot's starter set, lets the operator trim it in conversation, and queues the surviving apps as install jobs at finalize — foundations first, same order as above.

## What NOT to include

- No scripts.
- No scheduled_actions.
- No HEARTBEAT.md content.
- No openclaw.json fields.
- No requirements.integrations[] — integrations are required transitively through Calendar Sync.
example_triggers: Set up task tracking + meeting notes + pre-meeting briefs
Give me the full project-manager toolkit

test_cases.expected: Admin UI / installer resolves app_dependencies and installs all six downstream apps in topological order. After install, all six appear in the bot's apps list with status=active.

test_cases.trigger: What does the Project Pack include?
test_cases.expected: Bot reads this manifest's app_dependencies and reports: Meeting Note-taker, Commitment Tracker, Pre-Meeting Brief (behaviors) + Task Manager, Contacts, Calendar Sync (foundations).

trigger_recognition.pattern: Project Pack is a one-time installer. Mention it only when the user asks how to set up the project-manager toolkit, or when they ask which apps are bundled.

usage.how_to_use: Project Pack has no day-to-day runtime — it's an installer that brings in Meeting Note-taker, Commitment Tracker, Pre-Meeting Brief, plus the data-layer foundations. When the user asks about Project Pack, describe what's inside; direct them to the gallery install if they haven't installed yet.
bot_voice_examples: Project Pack bundles Task Manager, Meeting Note-taker, Commitment Tracker, and Pre-Meeting Brief — all installable as one.
You already have the project pack's apps installed.
To install Project Pack, run the gallery install from the Apps page.
